RagShortTexts: Silver strikes at Kutná Hora funded Přemyslid expansion, turning Bohemia into Europe's mint.

Variants.Content: Silver strikes at Kutná Hora in central Bohemia sparked a massive industrial silver rush. King Ottokar II codified mining privileges under the Ius Regale Montanorum, settling skilled Saxon miners who excavated shafts over a hundred yards deep with waterwheel hoists, minting millions of silver Prague groschen.
Silver bullion propelled Ottokar's bid for imperial dominance. His treasuries disbursed loans to Rhenish electors and hired mercenary cavalry, solidifying Přemyslid supremacy in Central Europe.
Miners wearing tallow lamps on leather caps chisel through granite ore faces underground. Smelting furnaces billow toxic smoke, yet refined ingots pour into royal casting troughs.
